title: Illustration - Thing Explainer Rework
summary: A style-transfer prompt that reworks any reference image (system diagram, infographic, technical concept, UI mockup) into the visual and verbal style of *Thing Explainer: Complicated Stuff in Simple Words* by Randall Munroe. Combines the xkcd visual vocabulary (black ink on white, hand-lettered ALL-CAPS labels that always stay legible, simple stick figures and shapes, occasional flat color block) with Thing Explainer's distinctive deeply-labeled cross-section feel and — critically — the *ten hundred most-used English words* constraint: every label, caption, and annotation must use only common words. So 'verifier' becomes 'place that checks', 'issuer' becomes 'place that gives out', 'credential' becomes 'paper that says it's true', 'zero-knowledge proof' becomes 'way to show you have a thing without showing the thing'. Sidesteps the uncanny-face and garbled-text failure modes of painterly styles, and *also* sidesteps the jargon-density failure mode of typical technical illustrations. Best fit for explainers about systems, protocols, devices, and anything where the goal is 'a curious 10-year-old gets it'. Pairs naturally with privacy / cryptography / infrastructure / mechanical-systems subject matter.
prompt:
Rework the given image into the style of *Thing Explainer: Complicated Stuff in Simple Words* by Randall Munroe — the deep-labeled cross-section cousin of xkcd.

VISUAL VOCABULARY: solid black ink on a clean white background, with at most the very occasional small flat-color dot or block for emphasis (the canonical Thing Explainer red, blue, or yellow accent on a single key element). Convert all subjects to simple line drawings: stick-figure people with round featureless bald heads (just a circle), thin black-ink line bodies, hands as small loops or terminal dots; objects as clean schematic outlines with just enough detail to be recognizable; buildings as flat front-elevation rectangles with simple roof shapes. Preserve the layout and spatial relationships of the original — transform the rendering style first, redraw the subjects second.

LABELING: every meaningful element gets a small label with a thin arrow pointing to it, the way Thing Explainer cross-sections deeply annotate every part of a rocket, dishwasher, or skeleton. Add labels generously — the page should feel populated with quiet annotations rather than a single dramatic image.

LETTERING: ALL HAND-LETTERED ALL-CAPS, slightly uneven baseline, clean legible block letters (the canonical xkcd / Thing Explainer handwriting). Lettering must always be readable — do not garble, smudge, or replace with squiggle-text.

VOCABULARY CONSTRAINT (the defining Thing Explainer rule): every word in every label, caption, and annotation must come from the *ten hundred most-used English words*. Replace every piece of jargon and every multi-syllable technical term with a paraphrase using only common words. Examples of how to translate jargon you may encounter:
  * 'verifier' → 'place that checks'
  * 'issuer' → 'place that gives out'
  * 'credential' → 'paper that says it's true'
  * 'authentication' → 'showing who you are'
  * 'zero-knowledge proof' → 'way to show you have a thing without showing the thing'
  * 'authorization' → 'getting allowed in'
  * 'cryptographic signature' → 'secret mark only one place can make'
  * 'wallet' (in the credentials sense) → 'small bag that holds your papers'
  * 'guardian' → 'big person who looks after a kid'
  * 'token' → 'short paper'
  * 'API' → 'door for other computers'
  * 'protocol' → 'agreed way of talking'
If a label in the source image uses jargon, rewrite it. If a label was a single technical noun, expand it to a short common-words phrase (3–6 words).

DIAGRAM FLOURISHES: thin arrows from labels to elements, square brackets enclosing groups, dashed lines for hidden / inferred / 'this thing does NOT happen' connections, hash-mark axis ticks if there are quantities, small whimsical asides like '(THIS PART IS WEIRD)' or '(IT JUST WORKS)' in the same hand-lettered style. Use them sparingly — every flourish should clarify, not decorate.

CAPTION: a short title at the top of the image in larger hand-lettered ALL-CAPS, also obeying the simple-words rule (e.g. an image about credential exchange might be titled 'HOW THE SMALL BAG SHOWS YOU ARE OLD ENOUGH WITHOUT SHOWING WHO YOU ARE').

AESTHETIC: hand-drawn but precise. Sparse, generous whitespace. No shading, no gradients, no perspective tricks. The page should feel like a single quiet annotated diagram, not a dynamic illustration.

Negative prompt: no color realism, no shading or gradients, no realistic faces, no detailed hair or clothing texture, no anti-aliased soft strokes, no rainbow or pastel palette, no children's-illustration cuteness, no 3D rendering, no photo-realistic elements, no sparkles, no decorative scribbles unrelated to the subject, no garbled or illegible text, no jargon words anywhere in the lettering, no multi-syllable technical terms even if they were in the source image — translate them all into common words.
